_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Peoples and Megaliths of Central Africa
910.label: Event
910.description: Hunter-gatherer Aka (BaAka) pygmy peoples inhabit the equatorial forests; early agricultural and iron-using communities emerge on the savanna.

910.name: Aka Forest Peoples
910.label: Event
910.description: BaAka pygmy communities in the southwestern rainforest practise hunter-gathering; among the earliest inhabitants of the region.

910.name: Bouar Megaliths (Tazunu)
910.label: Event
910.description: Megalithic stone monuments near Bouar; evidence of organised communities and ritual culture in western CAR.

920.name: Bantu, Sara, and Banda Migrations
920.label: Event
920.description: Successive waves of Bantu-speaking, Ubangian (Gbaya, Banda), and Sara peoples settle the savannas and river valleys; decentralised chiefdoms predominate.

920.name: Gbaya and Banda Settlement
920.label: Event
920.description: Ubangian-speaking Gbaya, Banda, and Ngbaka peoples migrate into the Ubangi-Shari region; slash-and-burn agriculture; small-scale iron smelting.

920.name: Zande and Nzakara Kingdoms
920.label: Event
920.description: Avongara-Zande expansion from the east creates hierarchical kingdoms in southeastern CAR; Nzakara sultanates develop court cultures.

930.name: Slave Raiding and External Predation
930.label: Event
930.description: The Ubangi-Shari region becomes a major slave-raiding zone; Sudanese, Wadai, and later Rabih az-Zubayr devastate the population.

930.name: Sudanese and Darfur Slave Raids
930.label: Event
930.description: Slave caravans from Darfur and Wadai prey on the peoples of the Ubangi-Shari savanna; dramatic population decline.

930.name: Rabih az-Zubayr's Raids
930.label: Event
930.description: Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr carves a slave-raiding empire across Ubangi-Shari and the Lake Chad region before French defeat.

940.name: French Ubangi-Shari (1889–1960)
940.label: Event
940.description: France establishes Ubangi-Shari as part of French Equatorial Africa; concessionary companies, forced labour, and the Kongo-Wara rebellion.

940.name: French Conquest and Concessionary Companies
940.label: Event
940.description: French outposts along the Ubangi River; vast concessions granted to private companies; rubber extraction through brutal forced labour.

940.name: Kongo-Wara Rebellion (War of the Hoe Handle)
940.label: Event
940.description: Gbaya prophet Karnu leads a widespread anti-colonial uprising against forced labour and head tax; brutally suppressed by French forces.

950.name: Independence and David Dacko
950.label: Event
950.description: Barthélemy Boganda's death in 1959; David Dacko leads independence; one-party MESAN rule; economic difficulties lead to military takeover.

950.name: Boganda, Independence, and Dacko
950.label: Event
950.description: Barthélemy Boganda champions independence but dies in 1959 plane crash; nephew David Dacko becomes president; single-party rule; France maintains military presence.

950.name: Bokassa Regime and Central African Empire
950.label: Event
950.description: Jean-Bédel Bokassa seizes power; self-crowns emperor in lavish Napoleonic ceremony; brutal repression; French intervention ousts him.

950.name: Bokassa's Military Coup and Rise
950.label: Event
950.description: Colonel Bokassa overthrows cousin Dacko on New Year's Eve 1965/66; escalating authoritarianism and personality cult.

950.name: Central African Empire Coronation
950.label: Event
950.description: Bokassa declares himself Emperor 1976; lavish coronation December 1977 costs a third of national budget; massacre of schoolchildren 1979.

950.name: Post-Bokassa Coups and Instability
950.label: Event
950.description: Cycles of coups (Kolingba, Patassé) and mutinies; French military interventions; democratic experiments repeatedly fail.

950.name: Kolingba and Patassé Eras
950.label: Event
950.description: Kolingba's military rule (1981–1993); Patassé elected but faces army mutinies and regional rebellion; Bozizé coup 2003.

960.name: Civil Wars and Séléka/Anti-Balaka Crisis
960.label: Event
960.description: Bozizé's rule ends with Séléka takeover 2013; Anti-Balaka reprisals; sectarian violence; French and UN interventions; Russian Wagner Group presence.

960.name: Bozizé Regime (2003–2013)
960.label: Event
960.description: General Bozizé seizes power from Patassé; peace agreements with northern rebels fail; Séléka coalition forms.

960.name: Séléka Takeover and Anti-Balaka Reprisals
960.label: Event
960.description: Séléka (Muslim coalition) seizes Bangui March 2013; Djotodia briefly president; Anti-Balaka (Christian/animist) militias retaliate; ethnic cleansing of Muslims.
